A1.justification: Both PDFs describe LangTime and TimePPO. Their main texts, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–C support reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments, fine-tuning comparisons, component ablations, sensitivity analyses, and zero-shot evaluations on Traffic and Illness.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds backbone controls, prompt-variation experiments, error analyses, transfer comparisons, and fine-tuning sensitivity studies.

M1.justification: The architecture, TCPs, and repeat-based TimePPO procedure remain. However, Equation (8) changes the maximized objective from adding a squared-error term to subtracting the Huber prediction loss. This substantively revises the stated alignment penalty, although the PDFs do not establish whether implementation or training runs changed.

E1.justification: The same nine datasets remain represented. Appendix C.1 extends zero-shot evaluation beyond Traffic and Illness to held-out Weather, Electricity, and ETT targets. This broadens the tested domain-transfer scenarios without introducing a new dataset family.

E2.justification: v2 adds TimesFM as an evaluated external comparator in Table 14. The comparator sets in the original main benchmark and Traffic/Illness zero-shot comparison remain unchanged. iTransformer becomes a cited source of baseline results, rather than an additional evaluated method.

E3.justification: The original benchmark settings remain, but v2 adds restricted-source pre-training protocols, backbone and prompt controls, final-segment error metrics, 5–20% fine-tuning data conditions, component-freezing experiments, and mask-rate/output-length grids. These substantially extend evaluation design. One new transfer protocol is inconsistently documented: Appendix C.1 names ETTh2, whereas Table 13 labels ETTm2.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained TCP/reward ablations and alpha/tau analyses, v2 tests GPT-2 and linear backbones, prompt paraphrases, beta/eta sensitivity, and final-step error accumulation. Appendix C adds transfer analyses, fine-tuning data-volume and component controls, and joint masking/output-length sensitivity. These address several previously untested questions about mechanism, robustness, and adaptability.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty intervals. Reported averages aggregate forecasting horizons; the additional experiments do not introduce statistical uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial numerical evidence in Tables 5–6, 8, and 13–17 and Figure 6. Original benchmark scores and retained appendix results are unchanged. Table 1 revises several win counts: fine-tuned LangTime changes from 49 in v1's table and 50 in its accompanying prose to 45 in both locations in v2.

T1.justification: Appendix A.1 corrects the small-error branches of both Huber definitions by restoring squared residuals in Equations (9)–(10). Equation (8) also corrects the penalty direction under maximization. These are limited mathematical corrections; no new theorem, proof, or formal guarantee appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: language-guided cross-domain forecasting, TCP-based alignment, TimePPO mitigation of autoregressive error, and strong benchmark and zero-shot performance. Added evidence does not redefine these core contributions.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands interpretation: it links final-step accuracy to sequence-wide return optimization, attributes GPT-2's shortfall to instruction following, and explains output-length and masking trade-offs. It also argues for applicability with limited fine-tuning data and TE-only updates. These mechanism and applicability discussions were absent from v1.

D1.justification: Appendix B.3 supplies exact instruction and background paraphrases for the new prompt tests. Figure 8 newly discloses attention softmax renormalization after hiding system and special tokens, and Table 1 changes the source attribution for borrowed results from TimesNet to iTransformer. Existing hardware, optimizer, principal hyperparameters, and code-access information remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for TimesFM, Chronos, GPT-2, linear forecasting, iTransformer, and additional forecasting research. Appendix C.1 adds positioning against large-scale time-series foundation models. Section 2's central account of prior alignment methods and RLHF remains essentially unchanged.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the introduction and model-analysis explanations, expanded captions, and new acknowledgements and an impact statement. Appendix B gains ablation details, while new Appendix C subsections precede the retained full results and cases. The original narrative and main section order largely remain.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is substantially redrawn to separate temporal extraction, multitask pre-training, and TimePPO fine-tuning. v2 adds nine tables and a beta/eta sensitivity figure, expands explanatory captions, and rearranges the experimental displays. Existing detailed result tables and forecasting cases are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the roles of the LLM backbone and TimePPO through backbone controls, final-step error evaluation, and additional transfer and fine-tuning studies absent from v1. Correcting the maximized objective's penalty sign and the Huber formulas also improves mathematical consistency. These gains outweigh the new ETTh2/ETTm2 labeling inconsistency, although neither version quantifies run-to-run uncertainty.
